main_body: Two-storey timber-framed house with a large hip roof of terracotta tiles, a plaster and timber front wall, three windows with flower boxes, a door, and hanging signs
top_band: Roof slope, rows ~4-43 at x=56: tile scallops alternating light orange (L~140) and dark plum (L~58). It is a large, clearly visible sloped roof surface, with a hip side slope on each side and a chimney. It ends at a dark eave row at rows 44-45 (L=15).
evidence: The roof reads as a big top slope seen from above, like the reference house roofs. A dark eave row (rows 44-45) sits between the roof and the front wall and shades the wall, which then runs to the base at about row 107. The wall carries inset timber framing, windows with sills and flower boxes, and a door, so the roof and the front wall are both clearly drawn. The roof covers about 40% of the height, matching the references. No receding isometric side faces appear; the hip slopes are roof surfaces.

style.evidence: Median colours per tile are 18, equal to house-h101_0 and above house-h112_0-stone (11). It has 191 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references, and 0% flat-fill coverage. Only 8% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown or plum beside the materials. The roof has per-tile highlights, the plaster is speckled, and the windows, flower boxes, signs and door each carry detail. The shading steps are comparable to the references, so it would sit next to them without looking thinner or more sticker-like.
